name: Juicy Fruit

tenures.note: Half of the Gay World Order's tag team Sweet Stuff (with Butt-A-Cup), managed by Coach Dike. Debuted 16 Dec 1997 beating the Horsemen's Tiny and Stupendous Steve for the EFW US Tag Team Championship; lost the titles back to the same team at the Season's Beatings PPV (29 Dec 1997).

caption: Half of Sweet Stuff, the Gay World Order tag team that held the EFW US Tag Team Championship for under two weeks in December 1997.

identity.note: Shares its ring name with juicy-fruit-aicw, a wrestler on a different, unrelated 1998 federation's own roster (a different corpus, different era, no overlap of feds, rosters, or documents). Stock tag-team gimmick name reused independently; no evidence of a shared referent.

name: Butt-A-Cup

tenures.note: Half of the Gay World Order's tag team Sweet Stuff (with Juicy Fruit), managed by Coach Dike. Debuted 16 Dec 1997 beating the Horsemen's Tiny and Stupendous Steve for the EFW US Tag Team Championship (pinning Tiny); lost the titles back to the same team at the Season's Beatings PPV (29 Dec 1997), pinned by Stupendous Steve's MoonPlex.

caption: Half of Sweet Stuff, the Gay World Order tag team that held the EFW US Tag Team Championship for under two weeks in December 1997.

name: Little Rich

tenures.note: Gay World Order member billed as the promotion's own cruiserweight talent, self-styled 'Little Dick Richards.' Made his EFW debut on 21 Dec 1997 against Horsemen enforcer Ice Century, losing by submission to the Hypothermia hold.

caption: Made his EFW debut for the Gay World Order on 21 December 1997, losing to Horsemen enforcer Ice Century.

name: Jolly Gay Giant

tenures.note: Led the Gay World Order's entrance on its 16 Dec 1997 EFW debut card; wrestled EFW's Dante to a double countout the same night, and entered the Season's Beatings PPV's ten-man battle royal (29 Dec 1997).

caption: Led the Gay World Order's entrance on its EFW debut and wrestled to a double countout the same night.

name: Coach Dike

tenures.note: Manages the Gay World Order at ringside from the stable's 16 Dec 1997 EFW debut through the Season's Beatings PPV (29 Dec 1997); featured in a limousine vignette with Little Rich delivering the group's own catchphrase ('When you're GWO, you're GWO... 4 Life!').

caption: Manages the Gay World Order at ringside across its December 1997 EFW run.

identity.note: Shares its name with coach-dike-aicw, a valet/manager on a different, unrelated 1998 federation's own roster (a different corpus, different era, no overlap of feds, rosters, or documents). Stock manager gimmick name reused independently; no evidence of a shared referent.

name: Kestral

tenures.note: Children of Darkness member and the reigning EFW Extreme North American Champion; retained the title against Tommy Grayson on 12 Dec 1998 after his stable ran in with chairs, then teamed with Krypt in a losing two-on-three brawl against the Privateers and a mystery partner (revealed as Grayson) on 23 Dec 1998.

caption: The Children of Darkness' reigning EFW Extreme North American Champion, who retained the title against Tommy Grayson with his stable's interference.

name: Krypt

tenures.note: Children of Darkness member, one half of the tag team of Krypt and Pariah, formerly two-thirds of the EFW Extreme Six Man Champions. Teamed with Pariah to beat Double Cross and SEXtreme in a three-way elimination tag on 12 Dec 1998; lost teaming with Kestral against the Privateers and Tommy Grayson on 23 Dec 1998, in a match Pariah missed after being unable to locate DarqueAngel, then argued with Pariah on camera afterward over the stable's internal tension.

caption: One half of the Children of Darkness tag team of Krypt and Pariah, formerly two-thirds of the EFW Extreme Six Man Champions.

identity.note: Shares its name with krypt, a WCOTW wrestler in a different, unrelated corpus and era (a 1998 Zeus-simulator-generated card); no shared operator, roster or storyline evidence. Stock gimmick name reused independently; never merged on name alone.

name: Pariah

tenures.note: Children of Darkness member, one half of the tag team of Krypt and Pariah, formerly two-thirds of the EFW Extreme Six Man Champions. Teamed with Krypt to beat Double Cross and SEXtreme in a three-way elimination tag on 12 Dec 1998; missed his scheduled 23 Dec 1998 tag match after searching all day for the missing DarqueAngel, arriving only at the end to accidentally chair-shot his own partner Krypt, then argued with him on camera over it.

caption: The other half of the Children of Darkness tag team of Krypt and Pariah, formerly two-thirds of the EFW Extreme Six Man Champions.

identity.note: Shares its bare ring name with pariah, an NFW wrestler in a different, unrelated corpus and era, and with pariah-lcw-mercury (aka Keith Summers), an LCW Mercury World Champion in a different, unrelated corpus and era; no shared operator, roster or storyline evidence with either. Stock gimmick name reused independently; never merged on name alone.

name: Despair

tenures.note: Children of Darkness member and former EFW Cruiserweight Champion (the title was retired rather than lost). Faced Razor Ron Jeremy for the EFW Extreme Television Championship on 12 Dec 1998 in a match with no finish, ended by his own stable's run-in against the Sinister Seven, which set up a Green Boot Match at Seasons Beatings 98; lost a bloody #1 contender's match to Tommy Grayson on 23 Dec 1998, ending his own run at a title shot.

caption: A Children of Darkness wrestler and former EFW Cruiserweight Champion who fell short of a Television Championship shot at Seasons Beatings 98.

identity.note: Shares its bare ring name with despair-rspwf, known only from later RSPWF Top 200 placings (2001-2004) tagged to other federations, and with despair-summit, a UeWF wrestler at the 1991 Summit of E-Wrestling; no shared operator, roster or storyline evidence with either. Stock gimmick name reused independently; never merged on name alone.

name: AsH

tenures.note: A three-time former EFW Cruiserweight Champion who left the Sinister Seven to join the Children of Darkness, accompanied by bodyguard Blaxe. Beat Billy Kane's opponent slot's expectations by losing a competitive match to him on 12 Dec 1998, then was forced into a reluctant tag with his rival Impaler against Unleaded and Glass Joe on 23 Dec 1998 -- a match Glass Joe won for his own side by chair-shotting his partner Unleaded and letting AsH finish Impaler, setting up an AsH-vs-Impaler #1 contender's match at Seasons Beatings 98.

caption: A three-time former EFW Cruiserweight Champion who left the Sinister Seven stable to join the Children of Darkness.

identity.note: Shares its ring name with ash-desmond-cswa (aka Ash Desmond), a 1999 CSWA wrestler, and with ash-rspwf, known only from a 2001 RSPWF Top 200 placing tagged to another federation (SPW); no shared operator, roster or storyline evidence with either. Stock gimmick name reused independently; never merged on name alone.

name: Blaxe

tenures.note: AsH's bodyguard and a named member of the Children of Darkness; accompanies AsH to the ring and helps restrain Death Inc's Casey Collins and Black Queen at ringside during AsH and Impaler's 23 Dec 1998 tag match.

caption: AsH's bodyguard and a member of the Children of Darkness.

name: DarqueAngel

tenures.note: Children of Darkness valet who escorts Krypt and Pariah to the ring and distracted the referee during Kestral and Tommy Grayson's 12 Dec 1998 title match; went missing before the 23 Dec 1998 show, which Pariah cites as the reason he arrived late to his own tag match.

caption: The Children of Darkness' valet, who escorts Krypt and Pariah to the ring.

name: Impaler

tenures.note: Leader of Death Inc. and one-third of the reigning EFW Extreme Six Man Tag Team Champions, a former two-time World Tag Champion, two-time US Champion, TV Champion and World Champion who disputes losing the World Title, carrying his own 'Death Inc. World Title' as what he calls the promotion's real championship. Forced into a reluctant tag with rival AsH against Unleaded and Glass Joe on 23 Dec 1998, lost when AsH turned on him with a chair at Glass Joe's urging, setting up an AsH-vs-Impaler #1 contender's match at Seasons Beatings 98.

caption: Leader of Death Inc. and one of the reigning EFW Extreme Six Man Tag Team Champions, who claims his own 'Death Inc. World Title' is the promotion's real championship.

identity.note: Shares its ring name with cwfpro-impaler, a 1998 CWF-Pro roster wrestler in a different, unrelated corpus, and with impaler-rspwf, known only from RSPWF Top 200 placings whose own 1998 entry tags this ring name to five federations including 'EFW' (verbatim, undifferentiated -- the held record's registry already documents five distinct 1997-98 entities sharing the EFW acronym). One shared axis (an undifferentiated acronym tag, no operator, host, date or roster detail) is not a join per the acronym-is-not-a-join gavel (2026-09-04); left distinct, but flagged here as a lead worth a second look if further evidence ties impaler-rspwf's 1998 EFW tag specifically to this wing rather than to efw-1-1997, efw-2, efw-0 or refw.

name: Unleaded

tenures.note: A former EFW World Champion who says the title was stolen from him in December 1997 and who won the Prince of Darkness rumble a second time, earning a World Title shot. Attacked an impostor sent out by champion Glass Joe on 12 Dec 1998; teamed with Glass Joe to beat AsH and Impaler on 23 Dec 1998, earning himself the singles World Title shot at Seasons Beatings 98 (a barbed-wire match) while AsH and Impaler were routed into their own #1 contender's match.

caption: A former EFW World Champion who won the Prince of Darkness rumble a second time to earn his shot at Seasons Beatings 98.

identity.note: Shares its ring name with unleaded-agw, an AGW World and TV Title holder in a different, unrelated corpus and era; no shared operator, roster or storyline evidence. Stock gimmick name reused independently; never merged on name alone.

name: Glass Joe

tenures.note: The reigning EFW World Heavyweight Champion and member of SEXtreme, who sent out a Mick Mann impostor in Unleaded's ring gear on 12 Dec 1998 before the real Unleaded appeared and attacked the impostor; forced by Paul E. Furiously to wrestle in a tag match on 23 Dec 1998 (teaming with Unleaded against AsH and Impaler) rather than face all three of his own #1 contenders at once, and won it for his side with a chair shot to his own partner Unleaded's back, setting up a Seasons Beatings 98 World Title defense against Unleaded in a barbed-wire match.

caption: The EFW World Heavyweight Champion heading into Seasons Beatings 98, where he defends the title against Unleaded in a barbed-wire match.

name: Mick Mann
caption: Ranked #25 in the RSPWF Top 300 Wrestlers for 1998.
notes: A placing in the RSPWF Top 300 Wrestlers, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own ranking poll, verbatim — Top 300 Wrestlers 1998 (30 August 1998): #25, with no federation named beside the entry.

tenures.note: "The Amazing" Mick Mann, a masked high-flyer from Venice Beach, California: challenged the Dragon for the Cruiserweight title in a steel cage at Extreme Halloween (4 November 1997), entered the Cruiserweight battle royal of 11 November, teamed with Glass Joe and a third partner as the Innovators of Violence against the HOA at the Survivor Series pay-per-view (1 December 1997), lost a loser-unmasks match to Patriot-X later that month and was billed in the four-way for the vacant Cruiserweight title at Seasons Beatings (29 December 1997); back a year later in SEXtreme with Glass Joe, teaming with Stupendous Steve on the Seasons Beatings 98 card (27 December 1998).
